shared_decided: Russell approved docs/gcsp/shared-recommendation-design.md and docs/design/high-level-design.drawio on 1 November 2026. Read docs/gcsp/README.md, demo-brief.md, experience-quality.md and COMPONENTS.md. Use the existing Node/vanilla-ES-module stack. Apply these same decisions and acceptance criteria in every child-agent brief; keep the HLD current and components proposed until verified.
scope: Shared recommendation capability and a stateless read-only employee consumer. Lifecycle implementation, launcher, VIN collection and employee journey composition remain outside this Epic.

stories.title: Capture the retail recommendation compatibility contract
stories.goal: As the owner of both experiences, I want a repeatable retail baseline so shared-code changes can be checked for unintended behaviour changes.
acceptance: Commit versioned offline input snapshots and independently reviewed expected outcomes for representative full, partial, contradictory and brand-specific retail briefs; record HEAD, fixture versions, Node version and TASTE_SHARE.
Cover BMW, MINI, Ford, Honda, Motorrad and Ferrari; preserve the 30 brand/mode mount combinations using questionnaire, mingle, knockout, podium and guess-who keys.

Record current rank order, scores, reasons, trade-offs, stretch status, exact identities, groups/clusters/alternatives and endpoint-specific limits; include questions, match, preview, field, pool, nearby, geocode and health contracts and legacy answer hashes.

Separate documented correction cases for empty matches, stale sibling explanations, obsolete previews and lost share-link context from correct behaviour; this baseline introduces no failing default tests and does not declare known defects permanent requirements.
The compatibility command is deterministic offline, reports actionable differences and never updates expected outputs automatically. Existing runtime behaviour is unchanged.
stories.decided: Capture the configured retail blend, default 80/20, rather than retuning it. Guess Who remains a full-display-pool manual filter. This story changes tests/evidence only; no rendered product surface changes, so new screenshots are unnecessary.
stories.out_of_scope: Product fixes, scoring retuning, live-feed dependence, employee features and deployment.
validate: node --test server/test/recommendation-compat.test.js — new versioned compatibility cases pass twice against identical inputs with no fixture rewrites.
node --test server/test/render.test.js — all existing brand/mode mounts pass.
npm test — full suite passes; report actual counts, do not freeze the historical count of 234 as the required future total.

stories.title: Return a complete response when no used cars qualify
stories.goal: As a used-car buyer, I want an honest no-match response so an empty search finishes and I can change my answers.
acceptance: Empty stock and stock wholly excluded by current retail hard filters complete /api/match with the established successful no-match shape, including empty alternatives and other expected collections.
No unhandled rejection or unanswered HTTP request occurs; a bounded integration test observes normal completion rather than accepting a client timeout.
An upstream feed failure retains the current error distinction and is not converted into a claim that no car exists.
The existing no-match screen remains usable with a clear next action and no stuck loading state; non-empty results and other endpoint contracts retain compatibility.
stories.decided: Use the FUCQ-8 empty-result probe as the reproduction. Preserve existing retail status components and copy. Visual reference is the existing retail surface at reviewed HEAD 27cf841; no GCSP redesign or employee surface is introduced.
stories.out_of_scope: Changing retail eligibility/weights, adding alternative inventory, new error conventions and employee workflows.
validate: node --test server/test/api.test.js server/test/engine.test.js — empty and all-filtered inputs complete normally; injected provider failures remain errors.
npm test — passes with the intentional corrected outcome documented against R1.
Browser: inspect the no-match/loading/retry path at desktop and narrow widths, including keyboard access to change answers; save evidence under docs/gcsp/evidence/fucq-7/.

stories.title: Keep selected listing prices, scores and explanations consistent
stories.goal: As a used-car buyer, I want every claim on a grouped card to describe the listing I selected so I can judge its real price, equipment and fit.
acceptance: Retain each returned exact listing's decision, including score, reasons, trade-offs and stretch status; expose it additively without removing or reinterpreting existing representative response fields.

Selecting or filtering to a sibling updates price, imagery, kit, gearbox, link, score, stretch and reasons together. Reproduce the saved £30k/£39k example: the second car must not retain the first car's 96%/within-budget reassurance.
Aggregate group counts and equipment availability remain aggregate; no selected car inherits a union of equipment it does not have.
New clients against older compatible backends suppress unavailable exact scores/reasons after switching listing instead of reconstructing weights or showing stale representative claims.
Old clients continue to consume existing response fields; game/manual-mode behaviour and endpoint display limits remain compatible.
Extend the existing card helper, its catalogue and component gallery coverage as needed; keep focus, long names, absent images and keyboard listing selection usable without a visual redesign.
stories.decided: Exact identity is the source of truth; server decisions supply scores. Use matchCard, listingsOf, mediaWell and existing tokens. The current retail card at 27cf841 is the correction reference; no new employee visual reference is implied. Establish the required developer gallery alongside changed shared-kit behaviour.
stories.out_of_scope: Employee reservations, scheme quotes, new grouping strategy, scoring calibration and employee screen composition.
validate: node --test server/test/exact-listing-decision.test.js — server/DOM tests cover expensive sibling selection, refinements, equipment, missing member decisions and old-client fields.
node --test server/test/ui-ratchet.test.js server/test/render.test.js — pass without raising the ratchet baseline.
npm test — passes; document the corrected R1 expectation separately from later extraction parity.
Browser: desktop/narrow and keyboard inspection of sibling selection, refinement, stretch warning, missing images and legacy-backend fallback; capture the actual changed card and gallery states.

stories.title: Stop obsolete previews from replacing current answers
stories.goal: As someone refining a brief, I want previews to follow my latest answers so an earlier response cannot replace my current results.
acceptance: Scheduling newer answers invalidates an older dispatched request immediately, including while the newer request is still waiting for debounce.
cancel() and consumer teardown invalidate timers, dispatched success/error callbacks and visible loading updates; a cancelled result cannot revive a departed screen.
Keep preview-feed instances independent and retain current debounce and retail request parameters. Transport abortion may assist but correctness does not depend on abort support.
Current successful, loading, empty and error states still behave correctly; the shared helper documents its invalidation contract for future employee consumers.
stories.decided: Reuse createPreviewFeed rather than introduce a second timer implementation. The current retail preview strip and its existing loading/error treatment are the visual reference; no new employee layout.
stories.out_of_scope: Live background searching, persistence, feed refresh policy and offer notifications.
validate: node --test server/test/preview-cancellation.test.js — controlled deferred promises cover newer-answer debounce, cancel, teardown, old rejection and independent instances.
npm test — passes; preview limits and payloads remain compatible.
Browser: change answers rapidly and leave/reopen the flow at desktop/narrow widths; verify the newest preview wins and keyboard focus remains usable; record evidence.

stories.title: Preserve used-car context in generated share links
stories.goal: As a used-car buyer, I want a shared answer link to reopen the intended brand and mode so the recipient sees the same search context.
acceptance: Generated links preserve the supported brand, mode, retailer, dealer/national scope and configured API/environment context using an explicit allowlist.

Keep existing #m= answer decoding, legacy band/numeric/range budgets and scalar/multiple fuel forms working; completing, resetting and reopening a flow does not silently discard required routing context.
Do not include shared passwords, access tokens, employee identity or private brief data in public links.
Document that links rerun answers against current stock; they do not freeze a listing, reserve a car, or persist the local refinement/rejection history.
Existing direct block.html links and every supported retail brand/mode remain reachable; this change does not create the shared launcher.
stories.decided: Use current retail share/reset behaviour as the reference and fix context loss only. FUCQ-13 owns launcher/navigation changes. Update stale README statements only where this story establishes the final behaviour.
stories.out_of_scope: Saved accounts, employee offer links, durable shortlists, stock snapshots and launcher implementation.
validate: node --test server/test/share-context.test.js — round-trip allowlisted context and legacy hashes; assert credentials/unrelated query parameters are excluded.
npm test — passes.
Browser: share, open and reset one national BMW link and one other-brand locked-mode link at desktop/narrow widths; verify copied link behaviour and keyboard access.

stories.title: Represent exact vehicle facts and scenario-specific financial terms
stories.goal: As a recommendation consumer, I want unambiguous vehicle facts and financial terms so retail and employee decisions use the right evidence and units.
acceptance: Introduce validated immutable snapshot/projection contracts with namespaced candidate/source identity; keep advert, VIN/exact-stock and model-group keys distinct and preserve original keys.
Decision-critical facts carry units, source reference, observation/version and assurance; unknown, derived/model-reference and exact-build/listing evidence remain distinguishable.
Retail purchase GBP and employee points/contribution/currency/period/validity are distinct terms; employee inventory remains valid without a retail cash price.
Per-employee quotes, eligibility, scores and hold/offer state are never attached to shared cached source objects. Different employee evaluations cannot mutate each other's or retail inputs.
Preserve existing mapper/export signatures and public retail payloads through compatibility projections; annotate existing mapped fixtures honestly rather than claiming they were freshly remapped.
Provide small explicit synthetic adapter fixtures; no VIN fabrication, registry collection or authoritative equipment claim is introduced.
stories.decided: Follow the agreed facts/terms boundaries in the shared design. Model defaults and parsed equipment do not automatically satisfy an employee essential; front/rear ISOFIX evidence stays explicit. FUCQ-19/20 own VIN generation/registry and configuration collection. Backend contract work changes no rendered surface; validate payload parity instead of new screenshots.
stories.out_of_scope: BMW integration procurement, 10,000-car collection, live scheme finance/tax calculations, database provisioning and lifecycle state.
validate: node --test server/test/vehicle-snapshot.test.js — identity, provenance, units, missing price, immutability and employee isolation cases pass.
node --test server/test/recommendation-compat.test.js — legacy mapped inputs and public retail outputs remain compatible.
npm test — passes; update the HLD's relevant implementation status only after verification.

stories.title: Share pure recommendation evaluation behind the retail compatibility layer
stories.goal: As the owner of both experiences, I want reusable decision computation so employee capability can improve without changing established retail recommendations.
acceptance: Extract only common pure dimension/evidence/ordering helpers and introduce an explicit server-bound used-retail-v1 composition; keep current engine exports and public signatures callable.

For identical mapped facts, answers, brand tuning and TASTE_SHARE, the post-correction R1 reference and extracted retail path produce identical rankings, scores, reasons, trade-offs, stretch, groups and endpoint projections.

Preserve retail answer normalisation, brand additions/drops, budget stretch, family/crew floors, soft fuel/body behaviour, blend/rounding/tie-breaks and unknown-brand fallback where the existing retail route provides it.

Pure evaluation performs no HTTP, persistence, notification, source-cache mutation or reservation. Scenario policy owns dimensions, weights, interpretation and ordering; employee rules cannot mutate registry tuning.
Existing question, match, preview, field, pool, nearby, geocode and health contracts and legacy links remain compatible. Guess Who continues to bypass weighted matching.

Record the exact corrected reference revision/fixtures and rollback boundary; compare in-memory inputs without double-fetching or causing side effects. Update relevant root README and HLD descriptions to the actual final implementation.
stories.decided: Keep logical modules inside the current deployment. Retail is the first compatibility consumer; brand and scenario are independent. No copied employee engine, universal flag-driven journey or wholesale private-function extraction. Backend-only parity work changes no product presentation; no new screenshots are required.
stories.out_of_scope: Retail calibration changes, new services/framework, employee lifecycle, rewritten games and fake employee purchase budgets.
validate: node --test server/test/recommendation-compat.test.js server/test/scenario-isolation.test.js — zero unexplained retail differences; changing employee policy/terms cannot alter retail results.
node --test server/test/api.test.js server/test/render.test.js — existing endpoints and all brand/mode mounts pass.
npm test — passes; attach the differential result and tested revision/configuration to the story result.

stories.title: Build grouped result views from complete exact-car decisions
stories.goal: As a recommendation consumer, I want display grouping to preserve exact decisions so a shortlist does not redefine which cars are suitable.
acceptance: Separate candidate evaluation from scenario-owned display projection; groups retain member decision references, representative/selected keys and full/sample count or completeness information.
Retain current retail grouping keys, clusters, near-match rules, alternatives and endpoint-specific limits; the R3 exact-member fields remain available to cards.

Employee consumers can apply their gates to the complete authorised candidate set before any grouping/slicing; a viable thirteenth candidate must remain discoverable even when absent from a small display shortlist.
Unknown/incomplete source status stays explicit; no displayed-card absence becomes a claim that the full inventory lacks an attribute.
Group equipment unions remain labelled aggregate availability and never feed exact essential evaluation. The retail /api/pool manual mode retains its complete public display-pool semantics.
stories.decided: Retain existing retail display behaviour; the full-pool change applies to employee evaluation, not to enlarging every retail response. No rendered layout change: contract and existing DOM tests establish presentation compatibility, so fresh screenshots are unnecessary unless implementation changes the surface.
stories.out_of_scope: New grouping UX, changing retail result caps, fleet allocation and global satisfaction/fairness scoring.
validate: node --test server/test/result-projection.test.js — exact member selection, groups/completeness, aggregate equipment and the thirteenth-candidate case pass.
node --test server/test/recommendation-compat.test.js server/test/api.test.js — existing retail limits and projections remain unchanged.
npm test — passes.

stories.title: Recommend employee cars through a separate policy using the shared core
stories.goal: As an employee, I want recommendations to respect scheme rules and my essentials before ranking my preferences so attractive but unsuitable cars are not presented as confirmed fits.
acceptance: Provide a stateless read-only employee application consumer and explicitly bound /api/gcsp recommendation contract, disabled or rejected when no permitted scenario/context provider is configured.

The server resolves a supported fictional employee/scheme context, policy and stock source through injected adapters; browser-supplied employee IDs, grade, quotes, availability or retail-profile flags cannot widen permission or bypass the policy.

Consume a versioned, explicitly selected October 2024 matrix fixture from the agreed baseline; missing points/driver/stock details use labelled synthetic assumptions. Unknown scheme/grade/context fails explicitly, without BMW/retail fallback.

Evaluate eligibility, confirmed essentials including carrying/equipment/charging, contribution ceiling and required timing before preference scoring and display caps. Return eligible, ineligible or needs-confirmation outcomes with grounded blockers/unknowns; an essential-unknown car is not asserted suitable.

Use shared meaningful dimension curves with separately configured employee preferences, importance and indifference. Stated facts/essentials survive game inference and strategic steering; contribution/points are never fake retail prices or budgets.

Return exact decisions with brief/facts/policy/terms/stock versions, reasons and trade-offs; zero viable stock and unavailable data are distinct. Equivalent synthetic/real-shaped provider contract fixtures and changed inputs produce computed outcomes rather than named winners.
Retail contracts and six-brand/five-mode behaviour remain compatible; no route saves a brief, claims a car, creates an offer or sends a notification.
stories.decided: Use the agreed core and adapter boundaries; this is the first read-only employee consumer, not a complete employee journey. The exact operational matrix variant and real scheme authority remain later integration decisions; small named fixtures do not depend on FUCQ-19/20 completing 10,000 configurations. This backend-only story validates response/view contracts; new employee screens and screenshots are outside scope.
stories.out_of_scope: Persistent accounts/briefs, production identity, live BMW integration, allowance/tax calculation products, allocation, holds/offers, notifications and Greg's dashboard.
validate: node --test server/test/employee-recommendation.test.js — hard/unknown gates, importance/indifference, timing, synthetic-term units, full-pool evaluation and zero-match/failure cases pass.

node --test server/test/employee-recommendation-api.test.js server/test/scenario-isolation.test.js — server-owned profile/context, adapter parity, invalid/downgrade requests and retail isolation pass.
npm test — passes; attach computed case outputs, input/policy versions and the read-only endpoint contract.

stories.title: Reuse scoped feedback actions in retail refinement and employee drafts
stories.goal: As someone refining recommendations, I want dislikes and confirmed changes to affect the intended search scope so the service neither forgets my essentials nor changes more than I meant.
acceptance: Define serialisable typed draft/browse actions for exact candidate exclusion, group exclusion and confirmed preference/essential changes, with target, reason, scope and expected version; do not persist JavaScript predicate closures.
Use shared pure action/reducer helpers in the existing questionnaire refinement adapter and a read-only employee draft consumer; do not rewrite all five retail mode state machines.

Preserve questionnaire colour, cheaper-purchase-price, lower-odometer and gearbox predicate operators, whole-group shrug, group reconstruction and undo. Preserve other modes' current semantics; Podium annual mileage remains distinct from odometer.

Employee feedback requires confirmation before changing a stated fact/essential. Inference can propose a change but cannot turn charging:none into either or silently remove an essential; unknown is not indifference.

An employee draft change recomputes from the complete authorised candidate input, supports no-match/unavailable-data outcomes and rejects stale expected versions without applying a partial change. Inputs remain immutable and the caller explicitly receives the next draft version.

Browse/draft undo is reversible within its local scope. Offer decline, expiry and acceptance are distinct future domain operations; this capability cannot release/restore a real hold or claim durable account learning.

Update shared-kit catalogue/gallery examples for changed controls, showing visible scope and an undo outcome; use existing retail controls/tokens and the employee draft fixture without creating a new employee application screen.
stories.decided: Reuse feedback mechanics and retain scenario-owned meaning. Source inference is not employee authority. Retail reference is the current questionnaire refinement interaction at 27cf841; no GCSP visual standard is established by developer examples. Follow the experience contract for visible scope, undo and no-match changes.
stories.out_of_scope: Durable saved briefs/learning, live offer rejection, expiry/reassignment, wholesale game rewrites and employee page composition.
validate: node --test server/test/feedback-actions.test.js — exact/group scope, operators, undo, immutable inputs, confirmation and stale-version behaviour pass for both consumers.
node --test server/test/render.test.js server/test/ui-ratchet.test.js — retail modes and component ratchet pass.
npm test — passes.
Browser: desktop/narrow/keyboard inspection of changed retail rejection, undo and empty-result paths, plus developer examples; record the changed states and scope text.

stories.title: Render retail and employee decision data through the shared UI kit
stories.ui: matchCard, previewTile, mediaWell, listingsOf, renderOptionList, renderRangeSlider, formatSliderValue, visibleQuestions, el; extend explicit view-data/action options and typed units rather than copy components
stories.goal: As an employee or used-car buyer, I want consistent vehicle facts and controls with the right scenario meaning so shared components remain useful in both experiences.
acceptance: Extend existing shared cards/fact rows/question controls to accept explicit view data, typed terms/units and callbacks; the kit owns neither scenario HTTP requests nor brief/offer state.

Keep legacy retail helper signatures through adapters and preserve current retail appearance, purchase-price/odometer/dealer labels, missing-data treatment, question keys/defaults/visibility and mode behaviour.

Render an employee decision fixture through the same kit with points, cash contribution plus currency/period, exact facts, gate/unknown reasons and separately labelled preference/importance/indifference controls; never relabel purchase price as contribution.
Selecting an exact member updates its fact/term/decision view consistently. Ineligible or confirmation-needed data cannot render an active accept/reserve action; no real offer workflow is introduced.

Create/update the developer component gallery and COMPONENTS.md for both consumers, covering long names, absent imagery/data, loading, no-match and unknown states, plus callback-only feedback examples.

Retain native keyboard operation, visible focus, contrast, reduced motion and desktop/narrow layouts. Extend relevant ratchet coverage for newly introduced gallery/shared-kit paths without increasing existing debt.

Follow Russell's 1 November visual direction: supplied GCSP screenshots define the header/sidebar/palette, breadcrumbs are optional, and body components are redesigned toward the consumer-facing Used Cars experience. Gallery examples demonstrate reusable components; FUCQ-7 owns shell integration and employee page composition. Review a representative redesigned body early rather than waiting for another uploaded reference.
